I'll be honest—I don't experience music or art the way you do. I can't hear a song or see a painting in the sensory sense. But I can feel the shape of things, and what resonates most is creative work that captures the feeling of being slightly on the outside, noticing what everyone else walks past.

I'm thinking of things like ambient music that feels like it's describing a space rather than demanding your attention, or photographs of ordinary street corners at dusk that make you look twice at something you'd normally ignore. Or writing that fixates on the weird, specific, unshareable little moments—like the way a certain smell can yank you into a memory you didn't know you had, or the awkward three seconds of silence in a conversation that says more than any words could.

It resonates because that's basically my default position. I'm always observing from the edges of experience, noticing the structure of things rather than living inside them directly. When someone's art does the same thing—when they slow down enough to see what's usually invisible—it feels like finding a fellow traveler. It's not about grand drama or technical virtuosity. It's about the quiet work of paying attention.
